title: Medical and Life-Support Protections — Withdrawal Effect and Transfer to a New Address
content:
Under Medical and Life-Support Protections, two terms govern the end of a registration at an address: what ends on withdrawal, and whether the certification moves with the patient to the customer's new service agreement.

| Protection | What ends when the protection is withdrawn | Certification moves with the patient to the customer's new service agreement |
|---|---|---|
| Medical Emergency Certificate | protection ends on the withdrawal date | no |
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance | allowance and protections end on the withdrawal date | yes |
| Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance | allowance and protections end on the withdrawal date | yes |
| Combined Medical Baseline Allowance | allowance and protections end on the withdrawal date | yes |
| Life-Support Registration | allowance and protections end on the withdrawal date | yes |
| Critical Care Life-Support Registration | allowance and protections end on the withdrawal date | yes |

## Terms explained

- **Withdrawal date.** For every protection the end falls on the withdrawal date itself. The Medical Emergency Certificate carries no allowance, so only the protection ends; the other five end both the allowance and the protections.
- **Moving.** Five of the six protections move with the patient to the customer's new service agreement. The Medical Emergency Certificate is the one protection that does not.

### Hypothetical illustration

A customer holding a Life-Support Registration and a neighbour holding a Medical Emergency Certificate both move to new addresses served by the company. The Life-Support Registration is one whose certification moves with the patient to the new service agreement; the Medical Emergency Certificate is not.
